_comment: Release cadence.. This belongs in react-native-releases long term so there is one copy; see the skill's open questions.
_cadenceRule: Releases ship on MONDAY, weekly. A release slips only when something blocks it and it then goes out on the first clear day after. Tuesday tags in the history are slips, not the schedule. Do NOT infer the next release date from the milestone dates below: derive it from the last actual publish date plus the Monday rule. 0.88.0-rc.0 (Tue 09-08) and rc.1 (Tue 09-15) were both one-day slips, rc.1 because Hermes picks were found missing.
_milestoneCaveat: branchCut and release are TARGET dates, not publish dates. They have been observed to drift: 0.87's golden target was 2026-08-10 but v0.87.0-rc.4 was tagged 2026-08-04. Treat them as planning targets only and derive the next release date from the last actual publish. The golden RC is expectedGoldenRc below.

series._releaseNote: Was 2026-10-05. Shipped Thursday 2026-10-15. rc.5 was cut on 10-12 with nothing in it, on a fixed expectedGoldenRc: 5 assumption, when rc.4 was already golden and 0.88.0 should have shipped that week. The rcHasContent gate exists so this does not repeat. rc.6 (10-14) then carried one pick after golden, the AssetRegistry TypeScript types (#1443), which is exceptional.
series._goldenByContentNote: The last RC by tag is rc.6, but rc.4 was the golden RC by content. Read as a prior, rc.6 would wrongly suggest 0.88 needed six RCs.

_goldenRcCaveat: A PRIOR, not a rule. The golden RC is whichever RC turns out to be last and that is decided by content, not by a number: the last RC that carried a real change was the golden one. History shows no fixed value (0.82 rc.5, 0.83 rc.5, 0.84 rc.5, 0.85 rc.7, 0.86 rc.3, 0.87 rc.4), so 4 is only a planning default for projecting dates. The rcHasContent gate is what actually enforces this: an RC with nothing in it means the PREVIOUS one was golden and the next action is promote to stable. rc.4 is the usual golden. A series can set goldenByContent when its last RC by tag is not the golden one, as 0.88 does.
_manualTestingNote: RC0 and RC1 always, plus the golden RC. Nothing else is manually tested. The stable .0 is promoted from the golden RC with nothing new in it, so it is covered. Patches are never manually tested. For a released series the golden RC is derived from tags. For one in flight it is expectedGoldenRc, treated as an assumption the captain can override.
